content: The risk of supervised models latching on to spurious features reinforces the need for interpretability. Although the development of supervised models is usually performance driven, placing more emphasis on interpretability could increase the adoption of these models in insight-driven analyses. One way would be to only use models that are already somewhat interpretable, for example models that use a small number of human-interpretable features. Rather than imposing such restrictions, there is also work on generating post-hoc explanations for individual predictions (e.g., BIBREF46 ), even when the underlying model itself is very complex.
